classification.difficultyReason: Verify the supplied cooling solution, identify ambient temperature and initial excess, calibrate k and solve a routine logarithmic time equation with seconds conversion.

content.prompt: A hot cup of coffee loses heat in a colder environment according to Newton's law of cooling, $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_E)$, where $T$ is the temperature of the coffee in degrees Celsius at time $t$ minutes, $T_E$ is the temperature of the environment, and $k$ is a positive constant.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $T=T_E+Ae^{-kt}$ is a solution of this equation, for any constant $A$.

answer.short: $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-Ake^{-kt}=-k(T-T_E)$, so the equation is satisfied for any constant $A$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{dt}&=-Ake^{-kt}\\-k(T-T_E)&=-k(Ae^{-kt})\\&=-Ake^{-kt}.\end{aligned}$$
Both sides are equal, so $T=T_E+Ae^{-kt}$ satisfies the differential equation for any constant $A$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: I make myself a cup of coffee that has already cooled from boiling to $90^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The temperature of the air in the office is $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What are the values of $T_E$ and $A$?

children.label: c
children.prompt: The coffee cools from $90^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $50^\circ\mathrm{C}$ after six minutes. Find $k$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find how long, correct to the nearest second, it will take for the coffee to reach $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}30&=20+70e^{-kt}\\10&=70e^{-kt}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac{1}{7}\\-kt&=\ln\!\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/7)}{-k}\\&=\frac{6\ln 7}{\ln(7/3)}\ \text{minutes}.\end{aligned}$$
This is approximately $826.78$ seconds, giving $13$ minutes $47$ seconds from when the coffee was at $90^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
